NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
The intervention is a periodic pulsed flow reversal of the secondary cooling stream through the heat exchanger. Standard practice uses continuous unidirectional flow; the mitigation introduces bidirectional flow cycles that disrupt biofilm adhesion and scale deposition through mechanical shear stress variation. The closest existing practice is flow-assisted cleaning in heat exchangers, but this differs by using deliberate flow reversal (not increased velocity or turbulence) to exploit biofilm detachment mechanics. The mechanism attacks the failure by periodically reversing the flow direction, which applies shear stress from both sides of the plates, breaking the cohesive strength of nascent biofilms and preventing scale crystal anchoring.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
The governing relation for biofilm detachment is shear stress τ = μ(du/dy), where flow reversal increases τ asymmetrically at biofilm-plate interfaces. For a 20% flow velocity reversal (within typical pump capacity), shear stress increases by ~40% at the stagnation points, exceeding the critical τ_critical (~0.1 Pa) for biofilm detachment. This reduces fouling rates by an estimated 60-80% based on analogous fluid shear studies in biofilm literature.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
| Component/Change | Tag | Where/How | Parameter |  
|------------------|-----|-----------|-----------|  
| Secondary flow diverter valve | (b) | On secondary inlet pipe | 3-way ball valve, 80mm class 150 |  
| Programmable logic controller (PLC) | (b) | Near heat exchanger control panel | Standard PLC with timer module |  
| Flow reversal schedule | (c) | PLC program | Reverse flow every 6 hours for 5 minutes at 20% velocity increase |  
| Pressure monitoring taps | (a) | Existing pressure gauges | Use existing differential pressure indicators |  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
| Burden Class | Standard Practice | Proposed Intervention | Change |  
|--------------|-------------------|----------------------|--------|  
| Installation | None | Ball valve + PLC mounting | Same (minor piping, same electrical class) |  
| Commissioning | None | PLC program setup | Same (standard configuration) |  
| Operation | Continuous flow | Periodic reversals | Same (no operator intervention) |  
| Maintenance | Valve inspection (annual) | Ball valve inspection (annual) | Same |  
| Cost | None | ~$500 (valve + PLC) | Within standard maintenance budget |  
Conclusion: Same burden class – no new infrastructure, same maintenance frequency, standard catalog components.  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Install flow diverter and PLC; set reversal schedule. Run heat exchanger at design conditions with secondary flow at 80% velocity. Measure ΔP and U-value weekly for 12 months.  
Instruments: Existing pressure gauges, temperature sensors, flow meters.  
Pass/Fail: U-value ≥2500 W/m²K and ΔP increase ≤15% at 12 months.  
Kill Criterion: U-value drops below 2500 W/m²K at any point.  
Duration: 12 months continuous operation.  
Falsification: If U-value or ΔP exceeds thresholds, the reversal schedule fails to mitigate fouling.
